question.:question/problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $y=2.$ Given that the point $P(-1,2,7)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=3{x}^{2}y$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P(-1,2,7)$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(-1,2).$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(-1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(-1,2) & =3(-1)^{2}(2)=6\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(3,-4) & =\frac{5(3)}{(-4)}-5(3)^2(-4)+4\cos(\pi (-4)) \\  & =(- \frac{15}{4})+(180)+(4) \\  & =\frac{721}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=2.$ Given that the point $P(2,3,8)$ lies on $C,$ and that $f_y = \dfrac{4x}y - 4x^2y+2\cos(\pi y)$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P(2,3,8)$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(2,3).$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(2,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(2,3) & =\frac{4(2)}{(3)}-4(2)^2(3)+2\cos(\pi (3)) \\  & =(\frac{8}{3})+(-48)+(-2) \\  & =- \frac{142}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
